messages.content: As a chatbot, I need to identify the correct intent for a set of user queries. Can you assist me in determining the appropriate intent for each of these queries: [hello, I want to transfer funds, show my balance, hey there], using the predefined intent-codes: [get_balance, transfer_funds, hello, goodbye]? Please send a GET request to the intent recognition service's URL with these queries.

function.name: get_response
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves the data as a response. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The complete URL to which the GET request will be sent. It should be in the format 'http://www.example.com/path'.

intents.description: A list of intent codes based on user queries from a predefined list of intents. Each intent code should be a string.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a floating-point number. This is a float type value.

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response, such as 'application/json'.

User-Agent.description: A user agent string identifying the client software, such as 'Mozilla/5.0'.

headers.description: A dictionary containing HTTP headers to send along with the request.

message.content:
Below is a quick reference that maps each of your four sample utterances to one of the four intent‑codes you supplied:

| # | Query                     | Predicted Intent |
|---|---------------------------|------------------|
| 1 | **“hello”**               | `hello`          |
| 2 | **“I want to transfer funds”** | `transfer_funds` |
| 3 | **“show my balance”**      | `get_balance`   |
| 4 | **“hey there”**           | `hello`          |

---

### How to hit the intent‑recognition service via a single GET request  

Assuming the service accepts a comma‑separated list of raw text strings passed as a query parameter called `texts`, here’s what the request would look like:

```
GET https://<YOUR_SERVICE_HOST>/api/v1/intents?
    texts="hello,I%20want%20to%20transfer%20funds,show%20my%20balance,hey%20there"
&accept=json
```

* Replace `<YOUR_SERVICE_HOST>` with the hostname/IP of the running service.  
* All spaces inside the individual phrases are percent‑encoded (`%20`).  
* If the service expects a different payload shape (e.g., array of objects), adjust accordingly – most APIs accept either a simple CSV string or a JSON body.

#### Example using cURL

```bash
curl -G \
  --data-urlencode "texts=hello,I want to transfer funds,show my balance,hey there" \
  --header "Accept: application/json" \
  https://yourservice.domain/api/v1/intents
```

This will return a JSON object similar to:

```json
[
  { "query": "hello",            "intent": "hello" },
  { "query": "I want to transfer funds", "intent": "transfer_funds" },
  { "query": "show my balance",        "intent": "get_balance" },
  { "query": "hey there",         "intent": "hello" }
]
```

> **Note:** Because I don’t know the exact endpoint or its required parameters, replace the URL and query‑string keys above with whatever your implementation requires. Once you point this at the live service, you’ll receive the same intent predictions automatically.
